title: No-three-in-line problem on the 75 x 75 grid
statement: Place as many points as possible on the 75 x 75 grid with no three on a line; at most 150 are possible. Solutions with 2n points are known for every n from 2 to 78 except 75 and 77; for n = 75 the best known has 148 points, from the 148-point set for n = 74 (Prellberg, 2026), which fits in the 75 x 75 grid. A set with more points improves it, and 150 would settle the cell.
submission: Text file: the points separated by whitespace, each written x,y with 0 <= x, y < 75.
score: the number of points (larger is better)

best_known.source: D(75) >= 148: the 148-point set for n = 74 (Prellberg, 2026), which fits in the 75 x 75 grid; A. Flammenkamp's no-three-in-line page lists no 150-point solution; Leaps in Bounds (github.com/daniel-munro/leaps-in-bounds), data at commit 4521e13 (8 Nov 2026) certifies 148; read 8 Nov 2026
